key_insight: Generating 3D human motions and 2D videos jointly yields better realism and consistency than treating them separately: 3D motions provide structural priors while pre-trained video models improve motion generalization, so co-generation unlocks mutual benefits.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between motion plausibility and visual realism by synchronizing 3D motion generation with realistic video synthesis, addressing inconsistent or implausible outputs when the two are created independently.
method: Coupled generation: run two video diffusion models (one biased toward 3D motion structure, one toward photorealistic video) in a co-generative framework to produce motions and videos simultaneously.
Cross-conditioning / bidirectional guidance: exchange signals between the motion and video models during sampling so each model informs and constrains the other for temporal and spatial consistency.
Leverage pre-trained video priors: use strengths of large pre-trained video models to improve motion diversity and generalization while keeping 3D structural constraints for plausibility.
impact: Enables more reliable end-to-end pipelines for animation, virtual avatars, and dataset synthesis by producing temporally consistent, physically plausible 3D motions tied to realistic video renderings; reduces manual cleanup and improves realism for downstream tasks.

paper_title: CoMoVi: Co-Generation of 3D Human Motions and Realistic Videos
paper_authors: Chengfeng Zhao, Jiazhi Shu, Yubo Zhao, Tianyu Huang, Jiahao Lu
